text: This is a sixteen-unit rent roll. Drop it in, and five seconds later you know it is leaking twenty-nine thousand dollars a year.
caption: Drop a rent roll in. Five seconds later: $29,280 a year, left on the table.

text: Most of America's small rental buildings are owned by individuals who price by gut, in a spreadsheet. LeaseLeak checks every unit against HUD's published Fair Market Rent for that exact ZIP code and bedroom count.
caption: Every unit is checked against HUD's Fair Market Rent for its ZIP and bedroom count.

text: Ember is the gap. Unit A one in Austin rents for seventeen fifty against a two thousand fifty benchmark. That's thirty-six hundred dollars a year on one door.
caption: Ember is the gap. Unit A1: $1,750 vs a $2,050 benchmark — $3,600 a year.

text: Timing matters too. Every ZIP gets its own seasonal curve from Zillow's rent index. A lease that ends in November re-signs at the bottom of the market.
caption: Each ZIP gets a seasonal curve from Zillow's rent index. November leases re-sign at the trough.

text: Three leases end in the next sixty days, and each one already has a renewal rent, capped at six percent so you keep good tenants.
caption: Three leases end within 60 days — each with a renewal rent, capped at 6%.

text: And the letters are written. New rent, never above the benchmark, and a term that ends in July, when Austin rents peak. Ten letters, one PDF, one click.
caption: Renewal letters, written: new rent, a term ending at the seasonal peak. Ten letters, one PDF.

text: There is no black box underneath. HUD's Small Area Fair Market Rents for thirty-eight thousand ZIP codes, Zillow's index for eight and a half thousand, and three lines of arithmetic. Nothing leaves your browser.
caption: 38,601 ZIPs of HUD data, 8,543 of Zillow, three lines of arithmetic. Nothing leaves your browser.

text: One honest limit: Fair Market Rent is the fortieth percentile, so this number is a floor, not an appraisal. Drop your own CSV or Excel file, any column names, and find out what yours says.
caption: Fair Market Rent is the 40th percentile — the number is a floor. Drop your own file and find out.
